Truck.title: Truck
Truck.description: Represents a truck in the SecureHaul system.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Truck entity.

currentLocationLatitude.description: Current latitude of the truck's location.

currentLocationLongitude.description: Current longitude of the truck's location.

idleTime.description: Idle time of the truck in minutes.

fuelLevel.description: Current fuel level of the truck.

loadWeight.description: Current load weight of the truck.

cargoIntegrity.description: Status of the cargo's integrity. This can be a string that represents different integrity levels (e.g., 'Good', 'Compromised').

Load.title: Load
Load.description: Represents a load posted by a shipper.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Load entity.

carrierId.description: Reference to Carrier. (Relationship: Carrier 1:N Load). Nullable until a carrier is assigned.

tripPlan.description: Trip plan for the load. This can be json.

Bid.title: Bid
Bid.description: Represents a bid made by a carrier on a load.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Bid entity.

submissionDate.description: Date when the bid was submitted.

VerificationDocument.title: VerificationDocument
VerificationDocument.description: Represents a verification document uploaded by a user.

id.description: Unique identifier for the VerificationDocument entity.

uploadDate.description: Date when the document was uploaded.

fileUrl.description: URL of the uploaded document file.

Subscription.title: Subscription
Subscription.description: Represents a user's subscription to a premium tier.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Subscription entity.

paymentMethod.description: Payment method used for the subscription.

User.title: User
User.description: Represents a user of the SecureHaul system.

id.description: Unique identifier for the User entity.

Driver.title: Driver
Driver.description: Represents a driver in the SecureHaul system. Inherits from User.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Driver entity. (Reference to User ID)

Shipper.title: Shipper
Shipper.description: Represents a shipper in the SecureHaul system. Inherits from User.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Shipper entity. (Reference to User ID)

Carrier.title: Carrier
Carrier.description: Represents a carrier in the SecureHaul system. Inherits from User.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Carrier entity. (Reference to User ID)

premiumMembership.description: Indicates whether the carrier has a premium membership.

FreightManager.title: FreightManager
FreightManager.description: Represents a freight manager in the SecureHaul system. Inherits from User.

id.description: Unique identifier for the FreightManager entity. (Reference to User ID)

companyName.description: Name of the freight manager's company.

EmergencyAlert.title: EmergencyAlert
EmergencyAlert.description: Represents an emergency alert triggered by a truck.

id.description: Unique identifier for the EmergencyAlert entity.

alertTime.description: Date and time when the alert was triggered.

alertType.description: Type of alert (e.g., 'Unauthorized Door Opening', 'Distress Signal').

locationLatitude.description: Latitude of the truck's location when the alert was triggered.

locationLongitude.description: Longitude of the truck's location when the alert was triggered.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore structure is designed to provide a secure, scalable, and easily maintainable database for the SecureHaul application. It prioritizes authorization independence by denormalizing access control data, enabling efficient security rules and atomic operations. The structure segregates data based on access requirements, leading to simpler and more secure rules. Consistent access modeling using path-based ownership and membership maps further enhances security and maintainability.

To achieve Authorization Independence (CRITICAL), the `Load` collection includes the `shipperId` which comes from the User document. The `Bid` collection includes the `carrierId` and the `loadId` which comes from the Carrier and Load document respectively. This eliminates the need for `get()` calls in security rules to check ownership or membership, ensuring atomic operations.

To achieve QAPs (Rules are not Filters), the data is segregated into collections based on ownership and access patterns. User-owned data like VerificationDocuments and Subscriptions are stored under `/users/{userId}` paths. Loads are directly stored in `/loads` and can be queried based on `shipperId` or `carrierId`.

Access Modeling:
- Path-Based Ownership: `/users/{userId}/verification_documents/{documentId}`
- Membership Map: Not explicitly used, but can be applied to collaborative features in future iterations.
- Global Roles: No global roles are used.

Denormalization:
- shipperId inside the Load document.
- carrierId inside the Bid document.
- loadId inside the Bid document.
